title: Sichos HaRan — teachings 291–300
notice: The supplied Hebrew texts are preserved independently. English is an editorial translation. Earlier English remains available as textual history.

globalQualifications.text: The unpointed and pointed Hebrew are preserved as independent supplied texts. The English follows the unpointed Hebrew; the source notes describe relevant uncertainties. Neither Hebrew text has been silently altered to agree with the other.
The English is an editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew. Earlier English is retained separately as historical wording, not as a second current translation.

References follow the detail supplied by the Hebrew. Additional explanations, identifications and more detailed references in the earlier English are retained as historical material; they have not been independently verified here.
These texts have not been verified against an original printed edition. Preserving the supplied spelling and vowel marks does not certify their accuracy.

fields.he: מצאתי בספר "לקוטי מוהר"ן" ענין אחד שלא נדפס עדין.
fields.he_nikud: מָצָאתִי בְּסֵפֶר "לִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן" עִנְיָן אֶחָד שֶׁלֹּא נִדְפַּס עֲדַיִן.
fields.en: I found in the book Likutay Moharan one matter that has not yet been printed.

history.earlier_supplied_English: This is from an unpublished manuscript from Likutey Moharan :

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The Hebrew says the compiler found a matter not yet printed; it does not specify a manuscript source.

fields.he: וזהו: דע – שבכל דור ודור נתחדשין בו חלאים חדשים רחמנא לצלן בבחינת (קהלת א): "יוסיף דעת יוסיף מכאוב".
fields.he_nikud: וְזֶהוּ: דַּע – שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר נִתְחַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ חֳלָאִים חֲדָשִׁים רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן בִּבְחִינַת (קֹהֶלֶת א): "יוֹסִיף דַּעַת יוֹסִיף מַכְאוֹב".
fields.en: And this is it: Know — that in every generation new diseases come into existence, may the Merciful One protect us, in the aspect of (Ecclesiastes 1): “Increase knowledge, increase pain.”

history.earlier_supplied_English: It is written, “Increase knowledge, increase pain” (Ecclesiastes 1:18) .

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: הינו מחמת שבכל דור שבא מאחר נתוסף הדעת של הפילוסופים כי בכל דור באים על חכמות חדשות, ועל ידי זה יוסיף מכאוב, שנתחדשו חלאים חדשים רחמנא לצלן. ה' יצילנו.
fields.he_nikud: הַיְנוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר שֶׁבָּא מְאֻחָר נִתּוֹסֵף הַדַּעַת שֶׁל הַפִּילוֹסוֹפִים כִּי בְּכָל דּוֹר בָּאִים עַל חָכְמוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה יוֹסִיף מַכְאוֹב, שֶׁנִּתְחַדְּשׁוּ חֳלָאִים חֲדָשִׁים רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן. ה' יַצִּילֵנוּ.
fields.en: That is, because in every later generation the knowledge of the philosophers increases, for in every generation they arrive at new forms of wisdom, and through this, “increase pain”: new diseases come into existence, may the Merciful One protect us. May God save us!

history.earlier_supplied_English: In every generation, new diseases come into existence. This is a result of the increase in knowledge. Each new discovery [based on philosophical and atheistic knowledge] results in some new pain. These are the new diseases that have come into existence. May God protect us!

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: ספרו לי שיחתו הקדושה שחסיד אחד בא לפניו שהיה חשוב קצת, וכבר היה בא בימים קצת, והיה לו ידיעה בכתבי האר"י ז"ל, ורצה להתקרב לרבנו ז"ל. והתחיל לדבר עם רבנו ז"ל, כדרך החסידים החשובים. ואמר לרבנו ז"ל: יורנו רבנו דרך לעבודת הבורא יתברך!.
fields.he_nikud: סִפְּרוּ לִי שִׂיחָתוֹ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁחָסִיד אֶחָד בָּא לְפָנָיו שֶׁהָיָה חָשׁוּב קְצָת, וּכְבָר הָיָה בָּא בַּיָּמִים קְצָת, וְהָיָה לוֹ יְדִיעָה בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ"י ז"ל, וְרָצָה לְהִתְקָרֵב לְרַבֵּנוּ ז"ל. וְהִתְחִיל לְדַבֵּר עִם רַבֵּנוּ ז"ל, כְּדֶרֶךְ הַחֲסִידִים הַחֲשׁוּבִים. וְאָמַר לְרַבֵּנוּ ז"ל: יוֹרֵנוּ רַבֵּנוּ דֶּרֶךְ לַעֲבוֹדַת הַבּוֹרֵא יִתְבָּרַךְ!.
fields.en: They told me his holy conversation: A somewhat notable chassid came to see the Rebbe, of blessed memory. And he was already somewhat advanced in years and was knowledgeable in the writings of the holy Ari, of blessed memory. Wanting to attach himself to the Rebbe, of blessed memory, he began to speak with the Rebbe, of blessed memory, in the manner of important chassidim, saying, “Would our Rebbe teach us the path to serve the Creator, blessed be He!”

history.earlier_supplied_English: A somewhat notable chassid 367 This individual was R' Yudel, who then became a lifelong follower of the Rebbe ( Kokhavey Or , p. 36, #23). He headed a large group of chassidim in Dashev, and when Rabbi Dov of Tcherin told him about the Rebbe, he came with his entire following ( Nevey Tzaddikim , p. 24). Rebbe Nachman received a blessing from him before his pilgrimage to Israel ( Tzaddik #32). See note 389. came to see the Rebbe. He was an older man and was knowledgeable in the writings of the holy Ari. Wanting to attach himself to the Rebbe, he began to speak in the manner of important chassidim, saying, “ Would the Rebbe teach us the path to serve God.”

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: ענה ואמר רבנו ז"ל, בלשון תמיהה: "לדעת בארץ דרכך"? (תהלים ס"ז) הינו מי שהוא עדין משקע בארציות גמור, הוא רוצה לדעת דרך להתקרב להשם יתברך?
fields.he_nikud: עָנָה וְאָמַר רַבֵּנוּ ז"ל, בִּלְשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָה: "לָדַעַת בָּאָרֶץ דַּרְכֶּךָ"? (תְּהִלִּים ס"ז) הַיְנוּ מִי שֶׁהוּא עֲדַיִן מְשֻׁקָּע בְּאַרְצִיּוּת גָּמוּר, הוּא רוֹצֶה לָדַעַת דֶּרֶךְ לְהִתְקָרֵב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ?
fields.en: The Rebbe, of blessed memory, answered in wonder and quoted the verse, “To know Your path in the earth?” (Psalms 67). That is, someone who is still “in the earth” — completely immersed in earthliness — wants to know the path to come close to God, blessed be He?

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe looked at him with wonder and quoted the verse, “To know Your path in the earth?” (Psalms 67:3) . The Rebbe meant that someone who was still “in the earth” – completely immersed in earthliness – wants to know the path to come close to God.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: וכפי המובן מהספור, שקפדתו היה מה שמדבר עמו בלשון גדלות שרוצה לידע דרך להשם יתברך כאלו לא חסר לו כי אם לידע דרכים, כי רבנו ז"ל, רצה שידבר עמו באמת.
fields.he_nikud: וּכְפִי הַמּוּבָן מֵהַסִּפּוּר, שֶׁקְּפֵדָתוֹ הָיָה מַה שֶּׁמְּדַבֵּר עִמּוֹ בִּלְשׁוֹן גַּדְלוּת שֶׁרוֹצֶה לֵידַע דֶּרֶךְ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּאִלּוּ לֹא חָסֵר לוֹ כִּי אִם לֵידַע דְּרָכִים, כִּי רַבֵּנוּ ז"ל, רָצָה שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר עִמּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת.
fields.en: And as is understood from this anecdote, the Rebbe was provoked because the man spoke to him in a haughty way, saying that he wanted to know a path to God, blessed be He, as if he lacked nothing but knowing paths; for the Rebbe, of blessed memory, wanted him to speak to him honestly.

history.earlier_supplied_English: We see from this anecdote that the Rebbe was provoked because the man spoke in a haughty way, saying that he was seeking the path to God as if he had already perfected himself to the extent that he lacked nothing else but to choose the appropriate path and walk up to God. The Rebbe saw through this and wanted him to speak to him honestly.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: שמעתי בשמו, מאיש אחד שדבר עמו. והזהירו להתפלל בכונה.
fields.he_nikud: שָׁמַעְתִּי בִּשְׁמוֹ, מֵאִישׁ אֶחָד שֶׁדִּבֵּר עִמּוֹ. וְהִזְהִירוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּכַוָּנָה.
fields.en: I heard in his name from a certain man with whom he spoke. And he admonished him to pray with devotion.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe once spoke to one of his followers about praying with devotion.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: ואמר לו: שכמו שהקול מעורר הכונה, כן להפך, הכונה מעורר הקול.
fields.he_nikud: וְאָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁהַקּוֹל מְעוֹרֵר הַכַּוָּנָה, כֵּן לְהֵפֶךְ, הַכַּוָּנָה מְעוֹרֵר הַקּוֹל.
fields.en: And he told him, “Just as the voice arouses devotion, so too, conversely, devotion arouses the voice.”

history.earlier_supplied_English: He said, “Voice arouses feeling. 368 Shelah , quoted in Kitzur Shulchan Arukh 6:1. The opposite is also true, for feeling can also arouse the voice.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
“Devotion” translates prayer intention, without identifying a particular theory of emotion.

fields.he: שכשמתפלל בכונה ונזהר להכניס כל לבו ומחשבתו בתוך דבורי התפלה, אזי ממילא יתעורר קולו להתפלל בקול כראוי. וכן נראה בחוש כמה פעמים.
fields.he_nikud: שֶׁכְּשֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּכַוָּנָה וְנִזְהָר לְהַכְנִיס כָּל לִבּוֹ וּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בְּתוֹךְ דִּבּוּרֵי הַתְּפִלָּה, אֲזַי מִמֵּילָא יִתְעוֹרֵר קוֹלוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בְּקוֹל כָּרָאוּי. וְכֵן נִרְאֶה בְּחוּשׁ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
fields.en: For when one prays with devotion and is careful to bring all one’s heart and thought into the words of prayer, then one’s voice will automatically be awakened to pray out loud as is proper. And this has been seen directly many times.

history.earlier_supplied_English: “Pray with feeling. Bring every thought and emotion into each word. Your voice will automatically be awakened and you will pray out loud.” This has been seen many times.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes repeated occasions without giving an exact count.

fields.he: שמעתי מפיו הקדוש: שבימי אלול שנוהגין ישראל לומר תקונים ותפלות ובקשות אחר התפלה וכו', ומאחרין יותר בבית הכנסת ובבית המדרש.
fields.he_nikud: שָׁמַעְתִּי מִפִּיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ: שֶׁבִּימֵי אֱלוּל שֶׁנּוֹהֲגִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹמַר תִּקּוּנִים וּתְפִלּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת אַחַר הַתְּפִלָּה וְכוּ', וּמְאַחֲרִין יוֹתֵר בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּבְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
fields.en: I heard this from the Rebbe’s own holy lips: During the days of Elul, Israel customarily recites tikkunim, prayers and petitions after the regular prayer, etc., and stays longer in the synagogue and study hall.

history.earlier_supplied_English: I heard this from the Rebbe’s own holy lips: It is customary to recite the Tikkuney Zohar as well as many prayers and petitions after the regular services during the month of Elul. It is also a custom to stay in the synagogue and study hall later than usual.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The Hebrew says tikkunim without naming a particular text.

fields.he: אמר: שמהנגון של התקונים ומה שהלב כואב וחלש מחמת שמתאחרין בבית המדרש, מכל זה נעשין דברים גבוהים וגדולים למעלה.
fields.he_nikud: אָמַר: שֶׁמֵּהַנִּגּוּן שֶׁל הַתִּקּוּנִים וּמַה שֶּׁהַלֵּב כּוֹאֵב וְחָלַשׁ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמִּתְאַחֲרִין בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ, מִכָּל זֶה נַעֲשִׂין דְּבָרִים גְּבוֹהִים וּגְדוֹלִים לְמַעְלָה.
fields.en: The Rebbe said that from the melody of the tikkunim and from the heart’s aching and weakness resulting from staying so late in the study hall, from all this great and lofty things are made above.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe said, “The melody of the Tikkuney Zohar and the fatigue resulting from staying so late in the study hall are all taken on high and made into great and lofty things” (see “ His Wisdom ” #127) .

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: שמעתי בשמו לענין התחזקות בתפלה, שאפלו אם האדם כמו שהוא, אף על פי כן יחזק ויאמץ את לבבו להתפלל להשם יתברך.
fields.he_nikud: שָׁמַעְתִּי בִּשְׁמוֹ לְעִנְיַן הִתְחַזְּקוּת בִּתְפִלָּה, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ אִם הָאָדָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוּא, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יְחַזֵּק וִיאַמֵּץ אֶת לְבָבוֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
fields.en: I heard in his name about encouraging oneself in prayer: Even if a person is as he is, nevertheless he should strengthen and fortify his heart to pray to God, blessed be He.

history.earlier_supplied_English: I heard that the Rebbe spoke of encouraging oneself in prayer as follows. No matter what you are, you can strengthen yourself and stubbornly pray to God.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: ואמר שיחשב בלבו: הלא אם אני רחוק בעיני מהשם יתברך כל-כך מחמת רבוי עוונותי, אם כן אדרבא עקר שלמות התפלה על ידי דיקא. כי הלא אמרו רבותינו ז"ל (כריתות ו:): 'כל תפלה שאין בה מתפלת פושעי ישראל אינה תפלה, וילפינן מקטרת שהיה בהם חלבנה'.
fields.he_nikud: וְאָמַר שֶׁיַּחֲשֹׁב בְּלִבּוֹ: הֲלֹא אִם אֲנִי רָחוֹק בְּעֵינַי מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל-כָּךְ מֵחֲמַת רִבּוּי עֲווֹנוֹתַי, אִם כֵּן אַדְּרַבָּא עִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הַתְּפִלָּה עַל יָדִי דַּיְקָא. כִּי הֲלֹא אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ ז"ל (כְּרִיתוֹת ו:): 'כָּל תְּפִלָּה שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ מִתְּפִלַּת פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָהּ תְּפִלָּה, וְיַלְפִינָן מִקְּטֹרֶת שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶם חֶלְבְּנָה'.
fields.en: And he said that one should think in one’s heart: Surely, if in my own eyes I am so far from God, blessed be He, because of my many sins, then, on the contrary, the essential perfection of prayer is precisely through me. For surely our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Kerisos 6b), “Every prayer that does not include the prayer of the sinners of Israel is not a prayer”; and they derive this from the incense, which included galbanum.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe said that you should think in the following manner: I may be far from God because of my many sins. Let it be. If this is so, then there can be no perfect prayer without me. The Talmud teaches that every prayer that does not include the sinners of Israel is not a true prayer ( Keritut 6b) . Prayer is like an incense offering. The Torah requires that the incense contains chelbanah (galbanum) (Exodus 30:34) , even though it has a vile odor by itself.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: ואם כן, אם אני בעיני כפושע ישראל ח"ו, אם כן אדרבא, כל שלמות התפלה על ידי דיקא וכנ"ל. ובודאי אני צריך להתחזק ביותר להתפלל להשם יתברך ולבטח בחסדי ה' שישמע ויקבל גם את תפלתי. כי אדרבא דיקא על ידי עקר שלמות התפלה, כי אי אפשר להקטיר קטרת בלא חלבנה.
fields.he_nikud: וְאִם כֵּן, אִם אֲנִי בְּעֵינַי כְּפוֹשֵׁעַ יִשְׂרָאֵל ח"ו, אִם כֵּן אַדְּרַבָּא, כָּל שְׁלֵמוּת הַתְּפִלָּה עַל יָדִי דַּיְקָא וכנ"ל. וּבְוַדַּאי אֲנִי צָרִיךְ לְהִתְחַזֵּק בְּיוֹתֵר לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלִבְטֹחַ בְּחַסְדֵּי ה' שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע וִיקַבֵּל גַּם אֶת תְּפִלָּתִי. כִּי אַדְּרַבָּא דַּיְקָא עַל יָדִי עִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת הַתְּפִלָּה, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַקְטִיר קְטֹרֶת בְּלֹא חֶלְבְּנָה.
fields.en: And if so, if in my own eyes I am like a sinner of Israel, Heaven forbid, then, on the contrary, all the perfection of prayer is precisely through me, as stated above. And certainly I must strengthen myself even more to pray to God, blessed be He, and trust in God’s kindness, that He will hear and also accept my prayer. For, on the contrary, the essential perfection of prayer is precisely through me, for it is impossible to offer incense without galbanum.

history.earlier_supplied_English: If I consider myself a sinner, then I am an essential ingredient of every prayer service. No prayer is perfect without me. I, the sinner, must strengthen myself even more to pray to God and trust that in His mercy He will accept my prayer. I am the perfection of the prayer – the chelbanah in the incense.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: נמצא שגם חלבנה היא שלמות הקטרת וכמו כן הוא לענין תפלה וכנ"ל, שבלא תפלתי הגרוע המצטרפת לתפלת ישראל לא היה שלמות להתפלה כמו קטרת בלא חלבנה וכנ"ל.
fields.he_nikud: נִמְצָא שֶׁגַּם חֶלְבְּנָה הִיא שְׁלֵמוּת הַקְּטֹרֶת וּכְמוֹ כֵן הוּא לְעִנְיַן תְּפִלָּה וכנ"ל, שֶׁבְּלֹא תְּפִלָּתִי הַגָּרוּעַ הַמִּצְטָרֶפֶת לִתְפִלַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא הָיָה שְׁלֵמוּת לְהַתְּפִלָּה כְּמוֹ קְטֹרֶת בְּלֹא חֶלְבְּנָה וכנ"ל.
fields.en: It follows that galbanum too is the perfection of the incense, and so it is with prayer, as stated above: without my deficient prayer joining the prayer of Israel, prayer would have no perfection, like incense without galbanum, as stated above.

history.earlier_supplied_English: Just like the vile-smelling chelbanah is an essential ingredient of the sweet incense, so my tainted prayer is a vital ingredient of the prayers of all Israel. Without it, prayer is deficient, like incense without the chelbanah .

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: בשעת התפלה, צריכין לקשר עצמו להצדיקים שבדור. כמובא בסימן ב' ובסימן ט' ב"לקוטי מוהר"ן" חלק ראשון ובשאר מקומות.
fields.he_nikud: בִּשְׁעַת הַתְּפִלָּה, צְרִיכִין לְקַשֵּׁר עַצְמוֹ לְהַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבַּדּוֹר. כַּמּוּבָא בְּסִימָן ב' וּבְסִימָן ט' בְּ"לִקּוּטֵי מוֹהֲרַ"ן" חֵלֶק רִאשׁוֹן וּבִשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת.
fields.en: During prayer one must bind oneself to the tzaddikim of one’s generation, as is brought in sections 2 and 9 of Likutay Moharan, Part One, and in other places.

history.earlier_supplied_English: In Likutey Moharan it is brought that one must bind himself to the tzaddikim of his generation ( Likutey Moharan I, 2:6, 9:4) .

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: על כן הזהיר לאנשיו שיאמרו קדם התפלה: הריני מקשר עצמי לכל הצדיקים שבדורנו.
fields.he_nikud: עַל כֵּן הִזְהִיר לַאֲנָשָׁיו שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ קֹדֶם הַתְּפִלָּה: הֲרֵינִי מְקַשֵּׁר עַצְמִי לְכָל הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבְּדוֹרֵנוּ.
fields.en: Therefore the Rebbe admonished his followers that before they began praying, they should say, “I am binding myself to all the tzaddikim of our generation.”

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe told his followers that before they began praying, they should say, “I am binding myself to all the tzaddikim of our generation.”

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: דבר עמנו כמה פעמים, שרצונו חזק מאד שנלך עם התורות שגלה. דהינו לילך תחלה איזה זמן עם תורה פלונית בערך ב' או ג' חדשים, דהינו שיהיו כל עבודתו והלוכו ביראת ה' על פי הנאמר באותה התורה, וכל תפלתו ושיחתו יהיה לזכות להגיע למה שנאמר באותה התורה, וכן יתנהג איזה זמן.
fields.he_nikud: דִּבֵּר עִמָּנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים, שֶׁרְצוֹנוֹ חָזָק מְאֹד שֶׁנֵּלֵךְ עִם הַתּוֹרוֹת שֶׁגִּלָּה. דְּהַיְנוּ לֵילֵךְ תְּחִלָּה אֵיזֶה זְמַן עִם תּוֹרָה פְּלוֹנִית בְּעֵרֶךְ ב' אוֹ ג' חֳדָשִׁים, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כָּל עֲבוֹדָתוֹ וְהִלּוּכוֹ בְּיִרְאַת ה' עַל פִּי הַנֶּאֱמַר בְּאוֹתָהּ הַתּוֹרָה, וְכָל תְּפִלָּתוֹ וְשִׂיחָתוֹ יִהְיֶה לִזְכּוֹת לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאוֹתָהּ הַתּוֹרָה, וְכֵן יִתְנַהֵג אֵיזֶה זְמַן.
fields.en: The Rebbe often told us that he very much wanted us to “go with” the lessons that he revealed. That is, first to go for a time with a particular lesson, for approximately two or three months: all one’s service and conduct in the fear of God should be according to what is said in that lesson, and all one’s prayer and conversation should be to merit attaining what is said in that lesson. And one should conduct oneself this way for a time.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe often told us that he very much wanted us to put into practice the lessons that he revealed. That is, “to go with a lesson” – for a time to base one’s entire service and approach to awareness of God on one lesson. Take a lesson and seek out its practical advice. Follow it for two or three months, making use of it to strengthen your devotion and fear of God. Pray to God and beg that He help you be worthy of attaining the ideal set forth in the lesson.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.
The Hebrew describes repeated occasions without giving an exact count.

fields.he: ואחר כך ילך איזה זמן עם תורה אחרת, וכן אחר כך, עד שיגמר לילך עם כל התורות. ודבר כמה פעמים מזה. אשרי מי שיאחז בזה.
fields.he_nikud: וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵלֵךְ אֵיזֶה זְמַן עִם תּוֹרָה אַחֶרֶת, וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ, עַד שֶׁיִּגְמֹר לֵילֵךְ עִם כָּל הַתּוֹרוֹת. וְדִבֵּר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים מִזֶּה. אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁיֹּאחֵז בָּזֶה.
fields.en: And afterward one should go for a time with another lesson, and likewise afterward, until one has finished going with every lesson. And he spoke of this several times. Happy is he who takes this to heart.

history.earlier_supplied_English: When you have completed one lesson, work on another. Continue this way until you have completed every lesson. Happy is he who takes this to heart.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: פעם אחת בא לפניו בערב יום הכפורים איש אחד מאנשיו שנחלש באותן הימים וספר לפניו צערו וחלשתו. ועמד שם עוד אחד מאותו העיר של זה האיש הנ"ל, שהיה אוהבו, ואמר לפני רבנו ז"ל, שחולאתו הכבידה עליו בשביל שהלך היום למקוה לטבל.
fields.he_nikud: פַּעַם אַחַת בָּא לְפָנָיו בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אִישׁ אֶחָד מֵאֲנָשָׁיו שֶׁנֶּחֱלַשׁ בְּאוֹתָן הַיָּמִים וְסִפֵּר לְפָנָיו צַעֲרוֹ וְחֻלְשָׁתוֹ. וְעָמַד שָׁם עוֹד אֶחָד מֵאוֹתוֹ הָעִיר שֶׁל זֶה הָאִישׁ הַנַּ"ל, שֶׁהָיָה אוֹהֲבוֹ, וְאָמַר לִפְנֵי רַבֵּנוּ ז"ל, שֶׁחוֹלַאְתּוֹ הִכְבִּידָה עָלָיו בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁהָלַךְ הַיּוֹם לַמִּקְוֶה לִטְבֹּל.
fields.en: Once on the eve of Yom Kippur, one of the Rebbe’s followers who had become weak in those days came before him and told him of his suffering and weakness. Another man from his town, who was his friend, was also standing there, and said before the Rebbe, of blessed memory, that his illness had become worse because he had gone to the mikvah today to immerse.

history.earlier_supplied_English: One of the Rebbe’s followers came to him on the day before Yom Kippur. The man had been very sick and told the Rebbe of his great suffering. One of his townsmen and good friends standing nearby said, “His illness has become worse because he immersed in the mikvah .”

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: ענה רבנו ז"ל ואמר: למה אתם תולים הכבדת החולאת במצוות, טוב וראוי יותר שתתלו בעברות.
fields.he_nikud: עָנָה רַבֵּנוּ ז"ל וְאָמַר: לָמָה אַתֶּם תּוֹלִים הַכְבָּדַת הַחוֹלַאַת בְּמִצְווֹת, טוֹב וְרָאוּי יוֹתֵר שֶׁתִּתְלוּ בַּעֲבֵרוֹת.
fields.en: The Rebbe, of blessed memory, answered, “Why do you blame the worsening of the illness on commandments? It is better and more fitting to blame it on transgressions.”

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe replied, “You blame the illness on a good observance. It is more fitting to blame it on sin.”

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.

fields.he: וזה היה בערב יום כפור האחרון של קדם הסתלקותו הקדוש באומאן.
fields.he_nikud: וְזֶה הָיָה בְּעֶרֶב יוֹם כִּפּוּר הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל קֹדֶם הִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בְּאוּמַאן.
fields.en: And this took place in Uman on the last eve of Yom Kippur before his holy passing.

history.earlier_supplied_English: This took place in Uman on the Rebbe’s last Yom Kippur.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
An alternative translation under this teaching number differs substantially from the supplied Hebrew. This translation follows the Hebrew rather than substituting that different account.
“In Uman” is linked here to the encounter; it may instead refer to his holy passing. The Hebrew does not settle the attachment.

fields.he: אחר שמחת תורה הייתי רגיל לבוא אליו ז"ל. ובכל שנה כשבאתי אליו אחר שמחת תורה שאל אותי: אם הייתי שמח בשמחת תורה?. וספר לי כמה פעמים איך היו העולם שמחים בביתו והיה לו נחת גדול מזה.
fields.he_nikud: אַחַר שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה הָיִיתִי רָגִיל לָבוֹא אֵלָיו ז"ל. וּבְכָל שָׁנָה כְּשֶׁבָּאתִי אֵלָיו אַחַר שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה שָׁאַל אוֹתִי: אִם הָיִיתִי שָׂמֵחַ בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה?. וְסִפֵּר לִי כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים אֵיךְ הָיוּ הָעוֹלָם שְׂמֵחִים בְּבֵיתוֹ וְהָיָה לוֹ נַחַת גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה.
fields.en: It was my custom to see the Rebbe, of blessed memory, every year after Simchat Torah. And every year when I came to him after Simchat Torah, he would ask me if I rejoiced on Simchat Torah. And many times he told me how the community celebrated in his house and how much pleasure he derived from their joy.

history.earlier_supplied_English: It was my custom to see the Rebbe every year after Simchat Torah. He would always ask me if I truly rejoiced on the festival. Many times he told me how the community celebrated in his house and how much pleasure he derived from their joy.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes repeated occasions without giving an exact count.

fields.he: וכן עוד פעם אחת באמצע השנה דבר עמי מענין שמחת תורה – אם אני מרגיש שמחה בלבי אז, או על כל פנים פעם אחר בשנה אם אני מרגיש שמחה בלבי.
fields.he_nikud: וְכֵן עוֹד פַּעַם אַחַת בְּאֶמְצַע הַשָּׁנָה דִּבֵּר עִמִּי מֵעִנְיַן שִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה – אִם אֲנִי מַרְגִּישׁ שִׂמְחָה בְּלִבִּי אָז, אוֹ עַל כָּל פָּנִים פַּעַם אַחֵר בַּשָּׁנָה אִם אֲנִי מַרְגִּישׁ שִׂמְחָה בְּלִבִּי.
fields.en: And likewise, once more, in the middle of the year, the Rebbe spoke to me about Simchat Torah: whether I feel joy in my heart then, or at least whether I feel joy in my heart at another time during the year.

history.earlier_supplied_English: Once in the middle of the year the Rebbe spoke to me about Simchat Torah. He asked me, “Do you now feel joy in your heart then? Or at least do you feel this happiness at another time during the year?”

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “then” in a conversation held in the middle of the year about Simchas Torah. Its precise time reference remains uncertain.

fields.he: (וברוך ה' שעזרני בחסדו הגדול לשמח בכל לב כמה פעמים בשנה, והרגשתי השמחה בלבי מה שאי אפשר לספר לחברו כלל. כי שמחת יהדותנו, מה שזכינו להיות מזרע ישראל ולהאמין בו יתברך, הוא לכל חד כפום מה דמשער בלבה. ואי אפשר לספר לחברו כלל. כמו שמבאר אצלנו כמה פעמים. בפרט בחינת הדבקות שמרגישין בשעת השמחה אפלו הפחות שבישראל, זה אי אפשר לספר כלל)
fields.he_nikud: (וּבָרוּךְ ה' שֶׁעֲזָרַנִי בְּחַסְדּוֹ הַגָּדוֹל לִשְׂמֹחַ בְּכָל לֵב כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים בַּשָּׁנָה, וְהִרְגַּשְׁתִּי הַשִּׂמְחָה בְּלִבִּי מַה שֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְסַפֵּר לַחֲבֵרוֹ כְּלָל. כִּי שִׂמְחַת יַהֲדוּתֵנוּ, מַה שֶּׁזָּכִינוּ לִהְיוֹת מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וּלְהַאֲמִין בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, הוּא לְכָל חַד כְּפוּם מָה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּהּ. וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְסַפֵּר לַחֲבֵרוֹ כְּלָל. כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים. בִּפְרָט בְּחִינַת הַדְּבֵקוּת שֶׁמַּרְגִּישִׁין בִּשְׁעַת הַשִּׂמְחָה אֲפִלּוּ הַפָּחוּת שֶׁבְּיִשְׁרָאֵל, זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְסַפֵּר כְּלָל)
fields.en: (And thank God, Who in His great kindness helped me to rejoice wholeheartedly many times during the year, and I felt the joy in my heart in a way that simply cannot be communicated to another at all. For the joy of our Jewishness — that we merited to be of the seed of Israel and to believe in Him, blessed be He — is for each person according to what he assesses in his heart. And it cannot be communicated to another at all, as is explained among us many times. Especially the clinging to God felt at a time of joy, even by the least among Israel, simply cannot be put into words at all.)

history.earlier_supplied_English: Thank God, in His great kindness, He helped me to rejoice wholeheartedly many times during the year. I felt a joy so great that it simply cannot be communicated to another. For the joy of being a Jew, of being of Jewish descent and believing in God, depends on how much one ponders it and cannot be expressed (see “ His Wisdom ” #1) . This is written about elsewhere. Especially the clinging to God at a time of joy, that even the least Jew feels, simply cannot be put into words.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.
The precise sense of the Aramaic expression about what each person assesses in the heart remains uncertain; it is not translated here specifically as an amount of pondering.
The Hebrew describes repeated occasions without giving an exact count.

fields.he: כי חפצו ורצונו היה מאד שנהיה שמחים בכל השנה כלה, בפרט בשמחת תורה ופורים ובשבת ויום טוב. וספר לי שפעם אחת בשמחת תורה רקד בעצמו לבדו בחדרו בלי סיועת אנשים אחרים.
fields.he_nikud: כִּי חֶפְצוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ הָיָה מְאֹד שֶׁנִּהְיֶה שְׂמֵחִים בְּכָל הַשָּׁנָה כֻּלָּהּ, בִּפְרָט בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה וּפוּרִים וּבְשַׁבָּת וְיוֹם טוֹב. וְסִפֵּר לִי שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת בְּשִׂמְחַת תּוֹרָה רָקַד בְּעַצְמוֹ לְבַדּוֹ בְּחַדְרוֹ בְּלִי סִיּוּעַת אֲנָשִׁים אֲחֵרִים.
fields.en: For the Rebbe very much desired and wanted us to be joyous all year round, particularly on Simchat Torah, Purim, Shabbat and festivals. And the Rebbe told me that once on Simchat Torah he danced all by himself in his room without the assistance of other people.

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe very much wanted us to be joyous all year round, particularly on Simchat Torah, Purim, Shabbat and festivals. The Rebbe told me that once on Simchat Torah, he was so overjoyed that he danced all by himself in his room.

required_qualifications.text: Editorial translation from the supplied Hebrew.

fields.he: פעם אחת אמר לי: כל מה שאתה רואה בעולם, כל מה שנמצא בעולם, הכל בשביל הבחירה והנסיון.
fields.he_nikud: פַּעַם אַחַת אָמַר לִי: כָּל מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה רוֹאֶה בָּעוֹלָם, כָּל מַה שֶּׁנִּמְצָא בָּעוֹלָם, הַכֹּל בִּשְׁבִיל הַבְּחִירָה וְהַנִּסָּיוֹן.
fields.en: The Rebbe once told me, “Everything you see in the world — everything that exists in the world — is all for the sake of free will and testing.”

history.earlier_supplied_English: The Rebbe once told me, “Everything you see in the world — everything that exists — is all for the sake of free will, in order to test people.” 369 See note 437. Also see Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzato, Derekh HaShem 1:2:4; Pischey Chokhmah VeDa'at #3.
